patch.value: GH-1628: preserve terminal timestamps for identical forced SDK updates

Reproduce direct SDK update and commitItemMutations in isolated non-Git trackers; Preserve both closure and mutation clocks for semantic no-ops; Retain legitimate terminal transitions and required force/ownership protection; Cover mixed batches retry idempotency and no-write negatives
A forced identical normalized update of an already terminal item preserves closure time mutation time and audit history across direct SDK and transaction paths.

value.text: Reproduced on current source (branch base 1a72d089d, built SDK): create closed item, then update(id, {title, status: closed, closeReason: same, force: true}) -> closureChanged=true, clockChanged=true (closed_at 00:17:26.978Z -> 00:17:27.105Z, updated_at -> 00:17:27.110Z). Open-item control with an identical payload: clockChanged=false. Root cause: routeCloseStatusUpdate in src/sdk/lifecycle/update.ts sends any update naming the close status to runClose without checking whether the item is already closed; mutateCloseMetadata then re-stamps closed_at unconditionally and closeItem passes no skipNoop, so item-store stamps updated_at. commitItemMutations reuses update(), so the transaction path shares the defect; update-many already compared before routing and was unaffected.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fix: routeCloseStatusUpdate now reads the stored item and, when the requested close status, trimmed reason and completed_at already describe it, applies only the remaining fields through the ordinary update path (skipNoop) and reports terminal_state_unchanged; a bare identical update returns changed_fields [] without force. A different reason remains a repeat closure routed to runClose with the existing force gate. After the fix the same repro reports closureChanged=false, clockChanged=false. Negative control: with src/sdk/lifecycle/update.ts stashed, 3 of the 4 new update-command tests fail (changed_fields [status, closed_at, close_reason] vs []); the fourth guards the preserved repeat-closure behaviour and passes both ways. Mixed-batch retry test on commitItemMutations keeps closed_at/updated_at byte-identical across two commits.

patch.value: A forced identical normalized update of an already terminal item preserves closure time, mutation time and audit history across direct SDK and transaction paths.

routeCloseStatusUpdate reads the stored item and, when the requested close status, trimmed reason and completed_at already describe it, applies only the remaining fields through the ordinary skipNoop update path and reports terminal_state_unchanged; a bare identical update returns changed_fields [] without --force. A different reason stays a repeat closure routed to runClose behind the existing force gate. The helpers live in src/sdk/lifecycle/repeated-terminal-state.ts; commitItemMutations reuses update() so transactions inherit the fix.

Reproduction against the built SDK: before the fix closureChanged=true/clockChanged=true, after the fix both false while the open-item control stays a no-op. Four update-command tests (forced identical, unforced identical with padded reason, other fields applied without re-stamping closed_at, different reason still routed) and one mixed-batch commitItemMutations retry test pass; with update.ts stashed three of the four fail. Linked test run recorded; docs/COMMANDS.md documents the receipt.
Identical terminal updates no longer re-stamp closure clocks

value.text:
Review follow-up on PR #1637 (CodeRabbit, 2026-10-31): two correctness gaps in the repeated-terminal-state no-op path, both fixed with regression tests.

1. **Blank reason under required-reason governance.** `describesCurrentTerminalState` normalized a whitespace-only `--close-reason` to "absent", so with `governance.require_close_reason` enabled an already-closed item answered `terminal_state_unchanged` while the same blank reason on an open item is refused with `close_reason_required`. The predicate now takes `requireCloseReason` and returns false for a supplied-but-blank reason only when a reason is required, so the close route refuses it. With the reason optional the blank value stays a no-op (routing it would re-stamp `closed_at`, the defect this item fixed).
2. **Concurrent reopen between classification and the field write.** The classification read holds no item lock. If another writer reopened the item before the title-only retry, the retry dropped `status` and the request reported `terminal_state_unchanged` on an open item. `applyRepeatedTerminalStateUpdate` now checks the status the locked write returned and hands a reopened item to the closure writer (`closeRoutedItem`, the same helper the ordinary route now shares), so the request is never silently downgraded.

Also covered: a changed `--completed-at` is a closure and its exact repeat a no-op; a routed close for a missing id refuses with the shared not-found guidance. `docs/COMMANDS.md` now states that other requested fields move `updated_at` and write history only when they change a stored value.

Evidence: `tests/unit/commands/lifecycle/update-command.spec.ts` (GH-1628 block, 8 cases) and module coverage 100% lines/branches for `src/sdk/lifecycle/repeated-terminal-state.ts`.

Review of the landing PR #1638 (CodeRabbit, 2026-10-31, rated Major): on a closed item, `--status closed --unset close-reason` took the repeated-state path and succeeded, removing a reason that `governance.require_close_reason` requires. `assertRoutedCloseKeepsRequiredReason` (in `repeated-terminal-state.ts`) now refuses such a request with the closure writer's own `close_reason_required` before either route can write, detecting the unset with the update parser's tokenization and the shared `CLOSE_REASON_UNSET_ALIASES`. The repeated-state path also re-checks the reason and completion time, not only the status, on the item the locked field write returned, and hands any divergence to the closure writer. Tests: "refuses unsetting a required close reason on a closed item before any write" (fails without the guard; bytes, reason and history unchanged) and "hands the request to the closure writer when the reason changed under the lock".
